title: Travelers Are Taking Trips Just to Buy Souvenirs
paragraphs: A simple shopping bag might not seem like something worth traveling for. But for some tourists, finding souvenirs like these is becoming an important part of their holiday.
This growing trend is called "pilgra-merch," a mix of the words "pilgrimage" and "merchandise." It involves traveling to particular places to buy items you can't easily find anywhere else.
According to travel company Skyscanner, 23% of travelers have taken a trip in the past year to buy something they couldn't get online.
And these items don't have to be expensive!

For example, shopping bags from the American supermarket chain Trader Joe's have become popular around the world. Videos of these bags have also become popular on TikTok, with views rising 167% between 2024 and 2025.
And despite all the attention they're getting, these mini tote bags cost just $2.99 each.
But why would someone travel just to buy a shopping bag?
Fashion psychologist Shakaila Forbes-Bell says this trend appeals to people she calls "sensation-seeking shoppers" — people who love finding new and exciting things.
For these travelers, buying something at the airport isn't enough. Finding a special item becomes a kind of mission, and completing that mission is part of the fun.
Forbes-Bell explains that this is because dopamine, a hormone in the brain linked to feeling good, is often at its highest before we buy something, not after.
In other words, planning a trip, looking for a certain shop and finally finding what you want can be more exciting than owning it!

There's also a social side to the trend. Having something that only a few, well-traveled people know about can make people feel they're part of a special group. Seeing someone else's Trader Joe's bag might make you feel connected to them, for example.
So while some people travel to see rare animals, climb tall mountains or visit historic sites, others are just as excited about finding a famous shopping bag!
